proposals.before: That same day Xiao Han, the Khitan-appointed governor of Bian, brought Duke of Xun Li Congyi to the Eastern Capital and asked him to take charge of the Southern Court's military and civil affairs.
proposals.after: That same day Xiao Han, the Khitan-appointed governor of Bian, brought Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, to the Eastern Capital and asked him to take charge of the Southern Court's military and civil affairs.
proposals.reason: Chinese 郇國公李從益 is title then personal name; idiomatic fuses them as "Duke of Xun Li Congyi".

proposals.before: Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites Bian Guangfan was appointed director of the court for the imperial clan.
proposals.after: Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites Bian Guangfan was appointed director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia.
proposals.reason: Chinese 衛尉卿 is the Court of Imperial Insignia/Guards director, not the imperial clan court (宗正卿); idiomatic conflates the two.

decisions.reason: The appositive form clearly separates Li Congyi's personal name from his title 郇國公 and reads naturally in English.
衛尉卿 heads the Court of the Imperial Insignia; the existing wording incorrectly identifies the separate court for the imperial clan.
